data.title: Neural Therapeutics Announces Anticipated Delay in Annual Filings and Application for Management Cease Trade Order
data.description:
Toronto, Ontario--(Newsfile Corp. - November 27, 2026) - Neural Therapeutics Inc. (FSE: HANF) ("Neural" or the "Company") announces that it anticipates being unable to file its audited annual financial statements for the year ended July 31, 2026, the related management's discussion and analysis and the related CEO and CFO certificates (collectively, the "Required Filings") by the prescribed filing deadline of November 30, 2026.

The anticipated delay is primarily attributable to additional accounting, financial reporting and audit work associated with the Company's acquisition of a 30.75% interest in CWE European Holdings Inc. ("CWE"). As a minority investor with significant influence but without control of CWE, the Company relies on CWE's management and financial reporting personnel for the timely delivery of financial information and supporting documentation. CWE's operations are principally conducted through subsidiaries in Germany, and differences in time zones, accounting systems and personnel availability have contributed to delays in obtaining, reconciling and reviewing the information required to account for the investment. CWE's management and financial reporting personnel continue to cooperate with the Company. The change of auditors during the financial year and changes in financial reporting personnel have also contributed to the timing of the annual reporting process. Management had expected to meet the filing deadline but, following a review of the outstanding work, concluded that the deadline was unlikely to be met.

The Company's auditors, Kreston GTA LLP, have commenced audit fieldwork. The Company has substantially completed its standalone financial reporting work and provided most of the information requested to date. Management is working closely with CWE and the auditors to complete the outstanding work and currently expects to make the Required Filings on or before December 31, 2026. The Company will file the Required Filings as soon as they are available. The completion date is an estimate and remains subject to the resolution of outstanding matters and completion of the audit. As a contingency, the Company is requesting that the principal regulator allow until January 29, 2027, if required.

The Company has applied to the Ontario Securities Commission, as its principal regulator, for a management cease trade order ("MCTO") pursuant to National Policy 12-203 - Management Cease Trade Orders ("NP 12-203"), as an alternative to a failure-to-file cease trade order against the Company. The MCTO, if granted on the terms requested, would restrict trading in securities of the Company by its CEO and CFO but would not generally prevent other shareholders from trading in the Company's securities. There is no assurance that the MCTO will be granted. If the MCTO is not granted and the Required Filings are not completed by the prescribed deadline, the applicable securities regulators may issue a failure-to-file cease trade order.

In support of the MCTO application, Northern Star Capital Inc., a shareholder controlled by the Company's CFO, has undertaken to advance up to $25,000 to the Company to fund outstanding audit fees, related filing costs and essential operating expenditures during the requested remediation period. The undertaking is conditional upon confirmation from staff of the Ontario Securities Commission that staff is otherwise prepared to recommend issuance of the MCTO, subject to confirmation of funding. The requisite funds would be advanced prior to issuance of the MCTO. No funds have been received pursuant to this undertaking as at the date of this release.

The Company intends to satisfy the alternative information guidelines under NP 12-203 for so long as it remains in default, including the issuance of biweekly default status reports in the form of news releases. The Company's directors and officers are subject to a trading blackout and will remain so throughout the default period, subject to the applicable policy and regulatory restrictions. The Company is not subject to any bankruptcy, insolvency or receivership proceedings. Other than the matters disclosed herein, there is no material information concerning the affairs of the Company that has not been generally disclosed.

About Neural Therapeutics Inc.

Neural Therapeutics is an ethnobotanical drug discovery company focused on developing therapeutic drugs for mental health conditions related to substance use disorders, including alcohol and opioid dependence. In August 2025, Neural completed the first stage of its investment in CWE, acquiring a 30.75% ownership interest in the company, which operates the Hanf.com retail and e-commerce business in Germany.

About CWE European Holdings Inc.

CWE, through its subsidiaries in Germany, operates the Hanf.com brand, including a network of specialty retail stores, e-commerce operations and a growing B2B business focused on CBD products, related wellness goods and accessories. Hanf.com operates 17 stores across Germany, including 15 company-owned locations and two franchised locations. Its operations are principally located in Germany, with a significant presence in Bavaria.

For further information

Ian Campbell, Chief Executive Officer

Neural Therapeutics Inc.

Forward-Looking Information

This news release contains forward-looking information within the meaning of applicable securities laws, including the expected timing of the Required Filings, the completion of the audit and outstanding CWE-related work, the requested MCTO, the conditional funding undertaking and the Company's intention to comply with the alternative information guidelines. These statements are based on management's current expectations and assumptions, including the timely availability and reliability of financial information, continued cooperation of CWE and the auditors, availability of resources, fulfilment of the conditions to the funding undertaking and completion of audit procedures. Actual outcomes may differ materially as a result of delays in obtaining information, additional accounting or audit requirements, funding constraints, the failure to satisfy the conditions to the funding undertaking, regulatory decisions and other risks described in the Company's public filings. There is no assurance that the Required Filings will be completed by the anticipated date or that an MCTO will be granted. data.title: Johannesburg picks Mashaba as mayor in ANC-backed deal
data.description:
Johannesburg city council elected Herman Mashaba as mayor on Friday, in a power-sharing deal which allows the once-dominant African National Congress to retain influence in South Africa's economic and financial hub.

No party won a majority in this month's local election and the coalition deal agreed by the ANC, Mashaba's party ActionSA, which came second and third respectively, and other parties, shuts out the pro-business Democratic Alliance, even though it won the most votes.

Although still revered by many as the party that ended apartheid, the ANC saw its vote share plunge in the November 4 elections, winning only 31% of votes nationally.

The coalition in Johannesburg, which has a council budget of nearly 100 billion rand ($5.8 billion), also includes the far-left Economic Freedom Fighters and uMkhonto weSizwe (MK).

A similar grouping will govern Tshwane, home to the administrative capital Pretoria, and Ekurhuleni, the Gauteng metropolitan municipality that includes O.R. Tambo International Airport.

Mashaba previously served as mayor of Johannesburg from 2016 to 2019 under the DA banner but fell out with the party. The city has churned through seven mayors since the 2021 local elections as successive coalition governments have unravelled.

The arrangement will test whether power-sharing can produce stable governance in South Africa's commercial capital, which is badly plagued by failing services and financial mismanagement after a decade of successive coalition governments which some activists say have allowed parties to evade responsibility.

ANC Secretary General Fikile Mbalula said on Friday the party had engaged with all political parties willing to meet it during coalition negotiations.

He said the DA was considered "a party of last resort", despite the two parties governing together nationally since 2024, when the ANC lost its parliamentary majority for the first time.

($1 = 17.3863 rand)

data.title: Canada Pumps Billions More For Battered Forest Industry
data.description:
By Paul Vieira

OTTAWA--Canada unveiled on Friday a multibillion-dollar plan to reverse the dwindling fortunes of the country's forest-products sector, which is struggling under the weight of U.S. tariffs and faces acute risks unless addressed.

Canada's Natural Resources Minister Tim Hodgson said the task at hand is to revitalize the sector and stop the flight of capital to the U.S. and elsewhere. Alongside hefty tariffs, Canadian officials acknowledged some of the forestry sector's challenges are homegrown, among them chronic underinvestment and regulatory overlap that thwarts access to cost-competitive fiber used in the production of pulp and paper.

For Hodgson's efforts, Canada has allocated an additional 6.5 billion Canadian dollars (US$4.5 billion) for forestry-sector improvements, building on C$3 billion provided in August 2025 to help with the fallout from U.S. tariffs. All told, the Canadian government has made available roughly C$33 billion in financing for all trade-exposed companies, and about C$10 billion in direct support for affected workers.

Most Canadian exports of softwood lumber - used in the construction of houses - face U.S. duties and tariffs of nearly 35%. Ottawa and Washington have engaged in a decades-long row about lumber products, with U.S. officials accusing Canada of unfairly subsidizing its forest industry.

Officials added forest-product exports have dropped 22% since President Trump imposed further duties on the sector. This has led to the closure of 12 Canadian sawmills, and output curtails in 40 other plants, the officials added.

Hodgson said the government wants to improve access to fibre, accelerate innovation in the sector, and drive domestic demand for Canadian forest products. "Business as usual is no longer an option for our forest sector," he said, adding the government's plan is meant to help the sector navigate current challenges and secure its future.

The additional money for Canada's forest sector is in response to findings from a government-appointed task force, which this year warned the industry faces an existential risk. "Continued inaction will accelerate capital flight, erode skilled workforces, destabilize rural and Indigenous communities, and forgo a generational opportunity to position Canada as a leader in the emerging global bioeconomy," the task force said.

Canada is home to nearly 10% of the world's forests, and about 40% of the country is covered by timberland. But the sector's economic heft has weakened considerably over the decades. Government data indicate that forest products account for about 1% of Canada's gross domestic product, down from a 3% level over two decades ago. Meanwhile, employment in the sector is about 40% below 2004 levels, and softwood-lumber production has declined by nearly a third from 2017 levels.

Of the C$6.5 billion made available, officials said about one-quarter of that cash will be focused on improving productivity at existing sawmills, while the remaining monies are expected to invest in new large-scale factories to accelerate the development of advanced forest products.

data.title: Basis steady while farmer selling stays quiet
data.description:
Spot basis bids for hard red winter wheat were unchanged in the southern US Plains on Friday while farmer grain sales were quiet, merchandisers said.

  • Cash trading was subdued after futures markets closed on Thursday for the US Thanksgiving holiday.

  • On Monday, the US Department of Agriculture is scheduled to issue a weekly update on condition ratings for the US winter wheat crop.

  • US hard red winter wheat export sales for 2026-27 were 172,277 metric tons in the week that ended on November 19, the USDA said.

  • Total weekly US wheat export sales were 564,683 metric tons, above analysts' expectations of 250,000 to 550,000 metric tons.

  • K.C. December hard red winter wheat (KWZ26) futures were 9 cents higher at $6.13 per bushel in afternoon trading. The contract rebounded after falling on Wednesday to its lowest level since February 17 at $5.97-1/2 a bushel.

data.title: Nvidia Faces Short-Term Washington Volatility, but AI Growth Story Holds Firm — Market Talk
data.description: Nvidia's multi-year AI growth thesis remains intact even as CEO Jensen Huang prepares to testify on Capitol Hill next week, Yorkville Ives's Dan Ives says. While Ives expects some short-term volatility ahead of Huang's congressional hearings, he maintains an outperform rating and a $250 price target on the stock. Ives dismisses recent bear arguments centered on regulatory scrutiny and Chinese export loopholes, estimating those sales represent "a containable 15% to 20% of revenue at most" and aren't factored into 4Q guidance. Even if 20% of planned data centers aren't built and Asia loophole sales disappear entirely, "we are still bullish on the thesis into the next two to three years," Ives writes, noting Huang "carries the weight of the entire tech sector and AI Revolution." (adriano.marchese@wsj.com)
